verdict.rationale: Databricks data is stored in Delta Lake (open, Parquet-based) format and can be accessed/extracted via Delta Sharing/OpenSharing (an open protocol for sharing data with non-Databricks users), the CLI, REST APIs, and SQL (databricks-docs-17, databricks-docs-56, databricks-docs-48). This gives a credible path to bulk-export and exit without vendor lock-in, but there is no single first-party guide titled 'export all your data and leave', and community comments note some governance/config friction (e.g. cross-cloud volume mounting limits) that could complicate a full migration (databricks-comm-5). Missing for 10: an explicit end-to-end 'full data export/exit' tutorial, and independent verification that a full account's data (tables, ML models, dashboards) can be cleanly exported in open formats without residual lock-in.
